bucket_id.description: The name of the logging bucket. Logging automatically creates two log buckets: _Required and _Default.
bucket_id.rationale: Bucket ID is a unique identifier for the resource. It has no security implications beyond being a reference name.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.description: An optional description for this bucket.
description.rationale: Description is metadata only and does not affect any security controls, encryption, or access policies.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

organization.description: The parent resource that contains the logging bucket.
organization.rationale: This identifies which organization owns the logging bucket. It has no direct security impact on the bucket's content or access controls.

retention_days.description: Logs will be retained by default for this amount of time, after which they will automatically be deleted. The minimum retention period is 1 day. If this value is set to zero at bucket creation time, the default time of 30 days will be used.
retention_days.rationale: Retention period must be sufficient for compliance requirements (CIS GCP Benchmark 2.3 recommends 30+ days for audit logs). Too short retention may result in loss of audit trails required for security investigations and compliance audits. Organization-level buckets often require longer retention (365+ days).

index_configs.description: A list of indexed fields and related configuration data.

index_configs.field_path.description: The LogEntry field path to index.
index_configs.field_path.rationale: Field paths determine which log fields are indexed for faster queries. This has no security implications as indexing does not expose additional data or change access controls.

index_configs.type.description:
The type of data in this index
Note that some paths are automatically indexed, and other paths are not eligible for indexing. See [indexing documentation]( https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/advanced-queries#indexed-fields) for details.
For example: jsonPayload.request.status
index_configs.type.rationale: Field type helps optimize indexing and query performance but has no security implications.
